message.content:
Colestipol tablets are a medicament in measured doses for retail sale, so they fall in heading 3004. Colestipol hydrochloride is a copolymer of diethylenetriamine and epichlorohydrin, a polymer with amine groups. Tablets of this kind are generally classified in 3004.90, "Other" medicaments. 3004.90.92 was the former "Other" subheading, and the more recent 3004.90.9290 is a statistical suffix.

I recall a CBP ruling on Colestipol hydrochloride tablets that classified them in 3004.90.9250 or thereabouts. The 3004.90.92 line reads "Other: Other: Other," with 9230 for antidiabetic and 9240 for others, though I am unsure of those. Older statistical suffixes under 3004.90.92 include 10, 20, 30 and others. The current 3004.90.92 breakdown has 3004.90.9215 for "Other," 9240 for "Cardiovascular drugs," and so on. I am not certain of that either, but "Other" is plausible, and 3004.90.9290 or 9255 may also exist. I will go with 3004.90.9290 as the best guess.
